title: Quadratic Equations: Completing the Square and the Quadratic Formula
seo_title: Grade 11 Quadratic Formula Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, by completing the square and by using the quadratic formula; solve equations in two unknowns, one of which is linear and the other quadratic.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 11 worksheets: completing the square, the quadratic formula and quadratic word problems. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Write the equation as ax² + bx + c = 0.
  • Quadratic formula: x = −b ± √(b² − 4ac)2a.
  • Completing the square: x² + bx = (x + b2)² − (b2)².
  • Reject answers that make no sense in a word problem.

Examples

Example

x² − 4x − 1 = 0

x = (4 ± √20)/2

Answer: x = 2 ± √5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Half the fractionDivide the whole top by 2a.
Only +There are two roots: ±.
Halving bTake half of b, then square it.

items.q: Write x2 − 16x − 8 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of −16 is −8. (x − 8)2 = x2 − 16x + 64, so subtract 64 to balance: −8 − 64 = −72. (x − 8)2 − 72.

items.q: Write x2 − 14x + 10 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of −14 is −7. (x − 7)2 = x2 − 14x + 49, so subtract 49 to balance: 10 − 49 = −39. (x − 7)2 − 39.

items.q: Solve x2 + 16x + 55 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move 55: x2 + 16x = −55. Add 64 to both sides: (x + 8)2 = 9. Square root: x + 8 = ±3, so x = −11 or x = −5.

items.q: Solve x2 − 16x + 48 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move 48: x2 − 16x = −48. Add 64 to both sides: (x − 8)2 = 16. Square root: x − 8 = ±4, so x = 4 or x = 12.

items.q: Solve x2 + 2x − 48 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move −48: x2 + 2x = 48. Add 1 to both sides: (x + 1)2 = 49. Square root: x + 1 = ±7, so x = −8 or x = 6.

items.q: Solve x2 − 8x + 7 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move 7: x2 − 8x = −7. Add 16 to both sides: (x − 4)2 = 9. Square root: x − 4 = ±3, so x = 1 or x = 7.

items.q: Solve x2 + 6x − 16 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move −16: x2 + 6x = 16. Add 9 to both sides: (x + 3)2 = 25. Square root: x + 3 = ±5, so x = −8 or x = 2.

items.q: Solve x2 + 10x − 24 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move −24: x2 + 10x = 24. Add 25 to both sides: (x + 5)2 = 49. Square root: x + 5 = ±7, so x = −12 or x = 2.

items.q: Write x2 + 8x + 9 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of 8 is 4. (x + 4)2 = x2 + 8x + 16, so subtract 16 to balance: 9 − 16 = −7. (x + 4)2 − 7.

items.q: Solve x2 + 2x − 3 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move −3: x2 + 2x = 3. Add 1 to both sides: (x + 1)2 = 4. Square root: x + 1 = ±2, so x = −3 or x = 1.

items.q: A garden is 5 m by 20 m. A path of the same width goes all round it, and the path has an area of 70 m². Find the width of the path, correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: (5 + 2x)(20 + 2x) − 100 = 70 gives 4x2 + 50x − 70 = 0. The positive root is 1,27 m.

Ethan cycles 12 km at x km/h. Cycling 4 km/h faster would save 1 hour. Find x, correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 12 ÷ x − 12 ÷ (x + 4) = 1 gives x2 + 4x − 48 = 0. The positive root is 5,21.

items.q: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle differ by 5 cm. Its longest side is 8 cm. Find the shortest side, correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: x2 + (x + 5)2 = 64 gives 2x2 + 10x − 39 = 0. Use the formula and take the positive root: 2,57 cm.

items.q: A garden is 9 m by 15 m. A path of the same width goes all round it, and the path has an area of 77 m². Find the width of the path, correct to 2 decimal places.

items.q: Ravi cycles 30 km at x km/h. Cycling 3 km/h faster would save 2 hours. Find x, correct to 2 decimal places.

items.q: The product of two consecutive positive whole numbers is 380. Find the larger number.
items.e: x2 + x − 380 = 0 gives (x − 19)(x + 20) = 0. x = 19 (the positive root), so the larger number is 20.

items.q: The product of two consecutive positive whole numbers is 650. Find the larger number.
items.e: x2 + x − 650 = 0 gives (x − 25)(x + 26) = 0. x = 25 (the positive root), so the larger number is 26.

items.e: x2 + 6x = 160 gives (x − 10)(x + 16) = 0. The positive answer is 10.

A rectangle has a perimeter of 44 cm and an area of 96 cm². Find the length of its longer side.
items.e: If one side is x, the other is 22 − x. x(22 − x) = 96 gives x2 − 22x + 96 = 0, so the sides are 6 and 16. The longer side is 16 cm.

items.q: A rectangular plot is 7 m longer than it is wide. Its area is 44 m². Find its length.
items.e: Width x m, length (x + 7) m: x2 + 7x − 44 = 0, so (x − 4)(x + 11) = 0 and x = 4. The length is 11 m.

items.q: The sides of a right-angled triangle are x cm, (x + 34) cm and (x + 36) cm. Find x.
items.e: x2 + (x + 34)2 = (x + 36)2 gives x2 − 4x − 140 = 0. The roots are 14 and −10; a length is positive, so x = 14.

items.q: The sides of a right-angled triangle are x cm, (x + 1) cm and (x + 9) cm. Find x.
items.e: x2 + (x + 1)2 = (x + 9)2 gives x2 − 16x − 80 = 0. The roots are 20 and −4; a length is positive, so x = 20.

items.q: A rectangular plot is 4 m longer than it is wide. Its area is 252 m². Find its length.
items.e: Width x m, length (x + 4) m: x2 + 4x − 252 = 0, so (x − 14)(x + 18) = 0 and x = 14. The length is 18 m.

items.q: A rectangular plot is 2 m longer than it is wide. Its area is 99 m². Find its length.
items.e: Width x m, length (x + 2) m: x2 + 2x − 99 = 0, so (x − 9)(x + 11) = 0 and x = 9. The length is 11 m.

items.q: The sides of a right-angled triangle are x cm, (x + 31) cm and (x + 32) cm. Find x.
items.e: x2 + (x + 31)2 = (x + 32)2 gives x2 − 2x − 63 = 0. The roots are 9 and −7; a length is positive, so x = 9.

items.q: A rectangle is (x + 7) cm long and x cm wide. Its area is 66 cm². Which equation is correct?
items.e: Area = length × width: x(x + 7) = 66. Expand and make one side 0: x2 + 7x − 66 = 0.

items.q: A rectangle is (x + 2) cm long and x cm wide. Its area is 37 cm². Which equation is correct?
items.e: Area = length × width: x(x + 2) = 37. Expand and make one side 0: x2 + 2x − 37 = 0.

items.q: A square lawn of side x m has a path 1 m wide all round it. The path has an area of 64 m². Which equation is correct?
items.e: (x + 2)2 − x2 = 64. The x2 terms cancel, leaving 4x − 60 = 0. Not every problem gives a quadratic.

items.q: The sides of a right-angled triangle are x cm, (x + 2) cm and (x + 7) cm, where (x + 7) cm is the longest side. Which equation is correct?
items.e: Pythagoras' theorem: x2 + (x + 2)2 = (x + 7)2. Expand and simplify: x2 − 10x − 45 = 0.

items.q: A square lawn of side x m has a path 2 m wide all round it. The path has an area of 176 m². Which equation is correct?
items.e: (x + 4)2 − x2 = 176. The x2 terms cancel, leaving 8x − 160 = 0. Not every problem gives a quadratic.

items.q: A rectangle is (x + 9) cm long and x cm wide. Its area is 105 cm². Which equation is correct?
items.e: Area = length × width: x(x + 9) = 105. Expand and make one side 0: x2 + 9x − 105 = 0.
